rules: A rejection, hold or refusal counts only through its declared mechanism and message.

Expected-success helpers turn the system's own declared refusal types into FAIL: ValueError from the reading interface, IntegrityError at load, AttestationRefused and RollbackDetected from the owner tool. Any other exception is an ERROR.
KILLED: at least one test that PASSES on the candidate FAILS on the mutant. CRASHED: no such FAIL, but at least one such test ERRORS. SURVIVES: neither. A crash is never a kill (ChatGPT round 2 #5).
Where exact_kill_set is given, the set of newly FAILING tests must equal it. Newly erroring tests are reported, never counted.
Mutants are built from the 'edits' below: each old string must occur exactly once in the candidate.
Exit code non-zero on any mismatch. The harness refuses to run if this file's sha256 differs from DECLARED_v0_8_7.sha256, or if the candidate differs from candidate_sha256_at_freeze.
Carried mutants use the same edits, applied as exact-once anchors on v0.8.7 (build_mutant refuses otherwise, at run time); re-anchored or renamed mutants say so.

v0.8.6 (process fix after three check-order mispredictions: T26 in v0.8.3; T57 and X10 in v0.8.5): every declared refusal in a new or corrected test records the line traced to raise it ('refusal_trace'), traced statically through the candidate before the freeze.
v0.8.7 (v0.8.6 DEVIATIONS): refusal traces cite the line of the raise statement, not the check's if line.
restore_ok is an expected-success helper: restore's refusal types (RollbackDetected, IntegrityError, AttestationRefused) become FAIL.

Threaded tests (T70-T72) re-raise any exception from a thread unchanged, so a crash in a thread is an ERROR, never a FAIL. Their only timing assumption is that B, if not blocked, finishes one dwell or one attest within 0.25 s.

candidate_only_checks run once, on the candidate only, after the suite, and are compared with their declared outcome (a mismatch counts). They are not run on mutants: S1 is a timed stress run, so a mutant's outcome there would not be deterministic. Their statuses enter the receipt.
controls_without_a_mutant: Checkpoint request built at signing time: OwnerTool.attest no longer accepts a request, so there is no line to remove. T27 exercises it.
render_consequence is display, not a control. T38 exercises it.
The owner tool's refusal of an organism keyed to another owner, and of a rewritten attested history: present in code, not exercised by any test this round.
fsync of owner and organism writes: not testable without a crash-injecting filesystem.
Recovery's refusal when a pending intent matches neither the organism nor the head: not exercised.
Recovery's refusal when the organism's saved state is unreadable: not exercised.
The owner's refusal when the previous crossing in a category is unknown to its ledger: not exercised.
The single clock reading in apply (expiry and record from one value): no test separates the two reads.
The owner's refusal wording (M, author A2): display only; tests match "owner's position".
load()'s refusal of a non-integer saved generation: not exercised.
_saved_generation's refusal of an unreadable saved state on save: not exercised.
hatch's early currency check ([HATCH-CURRENT]): _save's generation check refuses the same hatches, after the keys are generated.
_save's own unusable check: every save runs inside an operation whose currency check refuses an unusable object first.
load()'s and audit()'s organism lock: no test probes them (T69 probes the save and attest; T70-T72 the operation lock).
restore's refusals of an unreadable file, a file without a valid generation, another owner's organism, a prefix that does not replay, and a restored state that does not verify: not exercised.

T78_restore_after_lifetime_lapse.asserts: Genesis attested. A verbosity crossing is applied (unattested) and a formality reading is left pending. The owner's clock is set to the crossing reading's first signing plus twice the attested lifetime. attest raises AttestationRefused containing 'past its lifetime'. owner.restore(live object), through restore_ok, returns status 'restored'. The object is at checkpoint 0 with verbosity 0.5, mutation_sequence 0 and no pending readings; its last trace event is 'restored', naming a kept file that exists beside the state and whose sha256 equals the event's discarded_file_sha256. The witness is still at 0. A fresh load audits. A new verbosity reading on the restored object is then applied and attested (witness 1), and a fresh load audits.
T78_restore_after_lifetime_lapse.refusal_trace: attest -> verify_consequence -> _check_owner_acts: signed through this owner tool, then the lifetime check raises AttestationRefused 'past its lifetime' (L1965).

The kept bytes are written back (saved checkpoint 0). owner.restore raises RollbackDetected containing 'not the witness head'; the file is byte-identical afterwards; the witness is at 1.
T79_restore_refuses_when_saved_checkpoin.refusal_trace: OwnerTool.restore -> _recover (nothing pending) -> head_for -> _restore_attested: the file reads, its generation is valid, it is keyed to this owner, then the head check raises RollbackDetected (L1058).

T80_restore_refuses_a_rewritten_attested.asserts: Genesis attested; the live object dwells; attest (witness 1; the dwelling is inside the attested prefix). The dwelling's reason is rewritten in the saved file, the chain rebuilt and the seal recomputed (_reseal_attack, rechain=True). owner.restore raises IntegrityError containing 'attested prefix does not match the checkpoint'; the file is byte-identical afterwards.
